revisits.note: Removed the remaining Blender geometric pattern at its topology and sampling sources. The old OBJ repeated three new vertices for every triangle (139,600 faces / 418,800 vertices), so Blender saw isolated face islands; smooth shading could not cross them, and applying Ref's quad-oriented Catmull-Clark modifier pinched every island. OBJ export now deduplicates coincident positions and writes shared face indices, while the importer welds exact duplicates in already-downloaded legacy OBJ files before smoothing. Dense Hikari triangle hosts omit Subdivision and instead use a scale-aware Voxel Remesh at longest-edge/80 followed by six 0.5 Smooth iterations, which removes the remaining marching-grid corrugation while preserving the broad form. The Ref Empty absorption mask remains unchanged. Added an OBJ shared-topology regression and updated the Blender verifier to require connected vertices, all-smooth faces, the remesh/relax pair, no Subdivision, and linked Empty masks.

Corrected the Blender handoff against Ref/study_01_light_size05.blend after the first Bridge output exposed every imported OBJ triangle and generated the inclusion as a separate mesh. Host faces now all use smooth shading and receive the same Catmull-Clark Subdivision contract as Ref (viewport 1, render 2). Generated inclusions are now SPHERE-display Empty objects whose Object coordinates drive a 0.92145-to-1.0 density ramp in the host Volume Absorption, so they act as low-absorption regions inside one continuous surface rather than separate refractive bodies. Added a Blender-side verifier for this authored contract and retained the full source shape/material records as metadata.

Added the local Hikari Blender Bridge for the author's clarified division of work: Hikari is the quick instrument for sensing atmosphere, while Blender owns detailed forming and expression. After the existing five-file export completes, a new Mac button opens a narrowly scoped custom URL carrying only a sanitized case name. The author grants the export folder through the native macOS picker; the companion stages only the declared sidecar and mesh assets, uses its bundled validated importer, copies back a non-overwriting .blend, and opens it in Blender without a terminal command. The bridge remains a starting-state handoff, not a promise of pixel parity or finished Blender craft.

Added an optional local image/video background visualizer while preserving the existing procedural environment as the no-media default. Backdrop mode keeps the selected media screen-fixed and composes the existing transparent body, receiver shadow, ambient loss, and delivered-light field over it. Environment mode keeps that same visible backdrop but also maps the media directionally into body reflection and refraction; ordinary footage is accepted with a clear seam warning, while equirectangular footage is the intended seamless source. Media stays local to the browser session and is not embedded in .hkr. Static images remain compatible with Progressive Render; moving video intentionally keeps the view in Realtime Observation. Verified with the author's Ref portrait image and 3840-by-2160 MP4, including live frame changes in the body, removal back to the unchanged procedural scene, and no browser errors.

Corrected the packed-inclusion receiver behavior after the author pointed out that light transmitted through inclusions should reach the ground. The v0.30.0 safety stop was unnecessarily broad for equal-IOR low-absorption pockets. CPU and WebGPU receiver paths now preserve the outer-host refraction, measure the union length of every packed inclusion ball along the finite inside segment, replace that portion of host absorption with inclusion absorption, and deposit the resulting RGB throughput at the unchanged floor intersection. Overlapping balls in one soft cluster are interval-merged so light-path length is never counted twice. The receiver now labels this contribution as inclusion-transmitted light; different-IOR multiple-boundary refraction remains outside this equal-IOR contract.

Added deterministic volume packing for the physically important family of multiple inclusions. The author can keep the legacy single analytic inclusion or request 1–16 packed inclusions with a seed, mixed round/soft-cluster/stretched shapes, varied millimetre sizes, scattered/clustered/layered placement, minimum host wall, and minimum inter-inclusion gap. One shared generated OpticalScene now drives BODY display, .hkr persistence, validation, and Blender sidecar geometry. Packed inclusions are intentionally equal-IOR low-absorption pockets in one resin; the realtime BODY integrates up to 64 constituent balls as absorption voids. General multi-boundary receiver refraction is not approximated: packed mode labels the receiver as host-only and suppresses inclusion-caustic claims. Legacy single-inclusion receiver transport remains unchanged. Added deterministic replay, variation, containment, migration, and shader contracts; all 68 Hikari tests and the production build pass.

Corrected the expressive Stroke display after the author rejected v0.29.3: making the shadow darker or larger is wrong; the delivered light amount must remain unchanged while that light becomes many small random strokes. Removed the shadow-gradient ink entirely and deleted the detached lower-screen receiver plate. Stroke now leaves the same removed-baseline shadow, ambient loss, receiver domain, and transport endpoints as Composite. It gathers delivered RGB light in deterministic 4-by-4 receiver-texel blocks and redistributes each block's exact RGB sum onto one four-texel horizontal, vertical, or diagonal mark; the fixed block hash prevents temporal flicker. A pure reference test proves per-channel conservation and determinism, while shader contracts prevent shadow/backdrop reintroduction. All 66 Hikari tests and the production build pass. Same-camera WebGPU and SAFE browser comparisons show the same gray shadow with only the smooth delivered light changed into short marks; the detached blob is gone and no new browser warnings or errors appeared. Long authored arcs still require real mid-scale geometry rather than this display redistribution.

Added the first explicitly expressive receiver display named Stroke. It extracted dark shadow edges and warm delivered-light ridges and placed a cropped receiver plate below the body. The author rejected this v0.29.3 result on 2026-08-02 because it made the shadow darker and larger and produced a detached blob. It is retained only as a failed observation; v0.29.4 replaces it. This revision also added .hkr persistence and a repository/worktree/runtime version gate to prevent launching an older Hikari implementation.

Corrected the Blender backlight comparison after the author rejected the v0.29.1 broad-sun .hkr as too dark. Headless inspection of study_01_light_size05.blend showed that the rendered scene uses a gray World plus a 0.8-by-0.8 Emission plane at strength 5; its Area and Point lights are hidden. Resin_scatter has IOR 1.45, roughness 0.05, zero Volume Scatter density, and one material-coordinate mask that smoothly changes Volume Absorption density from 0.5 to zero, so the bright region is an equal-IOR absorption void rather than a nested refractive object or emitted glow. Realtime BODY and Progressive presentation now apply the renderer's linear-to-output colorspace transform exactly once, while accumulation targets stay linear. Equal-IOR inclusions bypass their nested interface and integrate a seven-sample smooth absorption mask matching the Blender ramp. Added a saved finite rectangular backlight emitter for this controlled BODY comparison and clearly separated it from the later physical west-sun/window room model; receiver/shadow transport does not yet consume that emitter. The revised .hkr uses Blender-matched IOR/roughness, zero inclusion absorption, calibrated host RGB coefficients, a finite backlight, and no direct sun. All 63 Hikari tests, production build, local WebGPU Realtime and 64-spp Progressive passed without browser warnings or errors.

Added a reproducible direct-sun/backlight diagnostic after the supplied dense-host case remained dark. The saved camera centre ray missed the 0.8 degree sun disc (1.114 degree centre separation versus a 0.4 degree radius), and even an exactly centred camera ray is displaced roughly 5–7 degrees by the irregular outer refraction. A one-action control now preserves target and camera distance while centring the direct background sun and explicitly warns that body refraction moves the sun image again. Added a validated 27.3 degree broad-source .hkr comparison that produces the Blender-like bright source and clear equal-IOR inclusion response without calling it a physical sun. Also corrected the unresolved outer-TIR realtime fallback so it never samples the outside environment with the pre-TIR incident direction. All 59 Hikari tests and the production build pass.

Integrated the existing MPM-to-Hikari artwork bridge into the current application shell. A dedicated Shape Deformation property starts the established CPU MLS-MPM study from the live Cloud Sculpt balls, formally selects OPTICS, updates only the realtime BODY at a bounded low rate through at most 220 coarse balls, and pauses receiver transport until author adoption. Input density is allocated under a 3,000-particle cap and shapes outside the finite MPM domain are rejected before allocation. BODY-only updates still refresh the OpticalScene containment state without starting receiver traces. Adoption records an explicit clear plus addBall snapshot in the normal Cloud history, so the selected instant reopens from .hkr without rerunning non-bit-deterministic simulation. Progressive Render, case save/open, Blender export, and Katachi edits are unavailable while shape evolution is active and resume after adoption; programmatic case/recipe restore also cancels a running preview. All 57 Hikari tests, TypeScript, and the production build pass. Real-browser WebGPU verification changed the initial 12-ball form to a 61-ball moving proxy while reporting receiver transport paused, adopted 59 balls, saved v0.29.0 as one timestamped .hkr containing 61 history entries, reopened the same 59-ball view, resumed the 65,536-ray receiver calculation, and produced no console warnings or errors. Mac screen recordings showed actual frame delivery ranging from 5.23 to 20.08 fps while the author found Windows GPU playback smooth, so realtime camera orbit and MPM playback now cap only high-DPI internal resolution at 1x and restore the normal ratio when motion stops; 1x Windows and SAFE rendering are unchanged. The August artwork schedule now places the black/white optical artifact gate before the first rough video take and freezes further MPM scope at this bridge until the optical gate passes.

Unified the visible background sun/area disc with the finite light's authored angular diameter. The former background used a fixed exponent and ignored sunSize, so broad-source receiver lighting and body refraction saw different emitter sizes. Natural and Analysis environments now use the same 0.1–30 degree diameter control as receiver light directions, while path depth, material absorption, and receiver energy accounting remain unchanged. Added a shader contract and recorded the supplied equal-IOR case as the fixed 0.53 versus 27.3 degree comparison.

Added the exact UTC save time, including milliseconds, to every downloaded .hkr filename while keeping the internal documentId stable. Repeated saves now remain identifiable revisions without relying on browser-added suffixes such as (1); the convention matches Progressive PNG timestamps. Recorded the author's supplied v0.28.1 case as an equal-IOR, zero-absorption inclusion setup whose muted background and large finite source help separate lighting conditions from the still-bounded nested BODY path.

Added a one-action inclusion control that copies only the outer host IOR, leaving inclusion hue, absorption, position, and size untouched. Extended both host and inclusion absorption authoring from 0–2.5 to 0–40 after reviewing the author's dark-purple and smoke-black Ref photographs: thick regions can now approach black while short illuminated paths retain transmitted color. Existing values and defaults are unchanged; the expanded range remains relative until physical scale and measured material coefficients are connected.

Reviewed and corrected the active Hikari schedule before continuing. Added a recording-oriented automatic camera orbit with Start/Stop, direction, and 10–180 second lap controls; it preserves OrbitControls target, horizontal radius, elevation, and lens. Orbiting is Realtime Observation only, manual camera input stops it, and Progressive RENDER is disabled until the camera stops. Added an independent inclusion transmitted-color picker while preserving the legacy neutral inclusion concentration exactly. The shared adapter derives complementary RGB Beer–Lambert coefficients consumed by BODY, transparent shadow, CPU/WebGPU receiver transport, saved .hkr settings, and Blender export; inclusion hue now participates in receiver scene revision. Added schedule, migration, camera-math, material propagation, and .hkr regressions.

Added a custom outer-host absorption color without treating it as surface paint. The author chooses the desired transmitted sRGB hue with a native color input, while the existing Absorption control remains the independent concentration. The OpticalScene adapter converts that hue continuously from neutral through pastel to saturated complementary linear Beer-Lambert RGB coefficients shared by Realtime and Progressive BODY rendering, transparent-shadow and receiver CPU/WebGPU transport, saved Hikari settings, and Blender export. Material settings are now part of the receiver scene revision, changing color invalidates any Progressive accumulation, and legacy documents normalize to the existing amber default. Custom inclusion absorption color and reproducible spatial color variation remain later material slices. Hikari tests passed 48/48 and the production build passed.

Added Progressive Render Phase 1 without slowing ordinary exploration. Realtime Observation remains the bounded interactive body view; an author-triggered RENDER action accumulates deterministic sub-pixel and rough-transmission samples into a linear half-float WebGL2 target at 16, 64, or 256 spp, then tone-maps the latest completed accumulation. STOP preserves that image, while camera, shape, material, daylight, receiver, backend, or viewport changes discard it and return immediately to realtime. The top bar owns RENDER/STOP, Calculation Status reports BODY / WebGL2 separately from the GPU / WebGPU or SAFE / CPU receiver backend, and fullscreen retains a STOP control. The BODY status exposes its actual target resolution; three HDR targets are capped to 2,560×1,440 equivalent pixels so a high-DPI or fullscreen display cannot consume unbounded integrated-GPU memory. Inclusion receiver-trust changes also invalidate the average, preventing samples from two scene states from mixing. PNG export captures the retained progressive image and identifies its spp in the filename, or exports realtime when no accumulation remains. Accumulation buffers, elapsed progress, and running state are derived runtime data and are not written into `.hkr`. This first phase improves anti-aliasing and rough optical sampling only; deeper host/inclusion path tracing and progressive receiver transport remain unimplemented. GPU and SAFE browser passes, 42 deterministic tests, the production build, and framebuffer review passed.

Restored the earlier continuous transparent-body appearance after the v0.25.2 bounded ambient fallback removed black islands but read as broad flat brown surfaces. Geometric normals remain authoritative for entry/exit medium decisions, while cosmetic normals remain limited to appearance. When the realtime view cannot complete a nested inclusion path within its bounded work, it keeps the already solved outer-host path. Outer-interface TIR gets one additional internal bounce; any still-unresolved body-view pixel then uses the earlier smooth host-looking environment approximation instead of black or flat pigment. This is an explicit body-view continuity approximation only: CPU/WebGPU receiver transport still rejects unresolved energy, and the v0.25.1 adaptive receiver reconstruction is unchanged. Added the dual-mode rendering decision to the implementation plan: immediate realtime observation while moving, followed by an author-triggered progressive still render that increases samples and path depth after the view stops. Shader contracts, 36/36 tests, production build, and local WebGPU visual verification passed.

Fixed the large black islands on the transparent body reported after v0.25.1. Cosmetic surface-normal variation had been reused for entry/exit refraction decisions, inventing broad unresolved/TIR regions; unresolved pixels then retained only a roughly four-percent Fresnel reflection and suppressed tint/haze, so a dark environment appeared as opaque black. View transport now uses unperturbed geometric normals while reflection, Fresnel appearance, and highlights retain the perturbed shading normal. Truly unresolved view rays keep known front reflection plus bounded host-tinted ambient instead of converting an implementation limit into black absorption. Receiver CPU/WebGPU transport and its energy ledger are unchanged. Added shader contract regressions; 35/35 tests, production build, WebGPU and SAFE body views passed locally without browser warnings.

Corrected the disconnected receiver-shadow islands reported from Windows SAFE mode. The energy-normalized receiver reconstruction radius now follows emitted sample spacing: 3 texels at 16,384 samples, 8 at 2,048, and a capped 12 at SAFE's 1,024 samples. Deposited light, shadow coverage, non-arrival light, and support expansion use the same radius, preserving integrated flux while removing visible point-pattern gaps rather than inventing optical detail. The Tokyo 17:00 isolated 2,048-ray reconstructed receiver-field comparison now passes all gates: 0.46% maximum RGB flux error, 0.27-texel centroid distance, zero-texel 95% envelope distance, 100% support IoU, 0.87% normalized deposit L1, and negligible coverage L1; raw-hit parity remains a separate future check. Hikari's top bar now persistently labels the actual execution backend as GPU / WebGPU, SAFE / CPU, CPU / FALLBACK, or backend ERROR. The label is also a one-tap mode switch; a validated one-use local handoff preserves the current recipe, settings, camera, document, and saved views across reload. Unit tests passed 33/33, production build passed, and local normal/safe browser switching passed.

Added an isolated author-triggered 2,048-ray CPU/WebGPU receiver parity runner. Headless exact-count builds do not publish textures, Analysis geometry, callbacks, pending state, or compute status; a dedicated comparison GPU avoids status and error-scope races, concurrent and stale jobs fail locally, and the report contains compact summaries rather than field arrays. The Tokyo 17:00 current scene measured 0.51% maximum RGB flux error, 0.20-texel centroid distance, 100% support IoU, 2.15% normalized deposit L1, and negligible coverage L1, while the 95% envelope remained five texels apart and intentionally fails the two-texel gate. The view shader now treats incomplete nested refraction and outer TIR as unresolved and renders only known front-interface reflection instead of invented host-only transmission. Added current-renderer-resolution viewport PNG export and the first editable multi-view `.hkr` JSON document with schema validation and legacy one-case import. Unit tests, production build, normal WebGPU shader compilation, parity isolation, multi-view recall, PNG generation, and forced-safe unavailability passed locally.

Added author-facing receiver diagnostics for Composite, Shadow coverage, Delivered light, and Non-arrival light without retracing or per-frame peak normalization. The transport field now stores spatial RGB non-arrival flux at each affected baseline position for material/interface loss, reflection, receiver/domain escape, and unresolved paths; support rejection remains separately identified. A persistent energy summary reports delivered, non-arrival, outside-support, and residual percentages. Recompute immediately suppresses stale Natural textures and Analysis geometry, GPU failure publishes an explicit CPU fallback, outer TIR no longer charges fictitious exit transmission, and unresolved inclusion-boundary paths can no longer fall through as host-only deposits. Added a pure CPU/WebGPU field comparator for revision/structure, RGB flux, centroid, 95% envelope, support IoU, and normalized spatial differences. Unit tests, production build, WebGPU shader compilation, all four modes, and no-retrace mode switching passed locally; the automated same-count device runner remains pending.

Replaced Natural's independent direct-shadow plus additive focused-light composite with paired receiver transport. CPU and WebGPU now consume the same seeded aperture and angular sun-disk samples; every affected ray records an unobstructed receiver baseline, refracted RGB throughput, and deposited point in a stable 28-float GPU payload. The fixed HDR receiver removes the affected baseline before adding transported irradiance, and transport-stage support containment prevents detached light outside the reconstructed shadow footprint. Runtime diagnostics independently accumulate material/interface loss, reflection, receiver escape, support rejection, and unresolved invalid paths instead of filling the ledger residual after the fact. The author-facing Natural view no longer applies decorative five-band offsets, caustic gain, recoloring, peak compression, or a second shader mask to reference transport; those expressive controls remain Analysis-only. Deterministic tests cover shared source samples, angular distribution, GPU payload stride, scalar/RGB flux conservation, paired replacement, absorption monotonicity, fixed bounds, support rejection, and ledger residual. Normal and forced-safe local browser checks passed without warnings. Automated full-field device parity and a receiver diagnostic overlay remain pending.

Replaced the per-frame reframed, peak-normalized 8-bit focused-light texture with a fixed 32×32 receiver study area sampled at 512² Float32 flux. CPU and WebGPU now weight deposits by emitted aperture area/sample count, include the same host absorption and interface loss, preserve flux through bilinear deposition and edge-normalized blur, and normalize the five spectral bands per RGB channel. The forced-safe CPU reference now uses up to 2,048 transport samples while keeping visible diagnostic geometry bounded. Deterministic tests cover flux conservation, sample-count and grid invariance, absorption monotonicity, fixed bounds, support rejection, spectral normalization, and ledger residual. Tokyo 09:00/12:00/17:00 WebGPU and the 17:00 CPU fallback passed locally without a detached bright patch; at 17:00 total CPU/WebGPU flux differed by 0.78% and centroids by 0.18 shape unit. Identical finite-light samples, baseline replacement, runtime energy-ledger closure, and a strict parity gate remain pending.

Corrected the detached focused-light patch reported in the Tokyo 17:00 Natural view. Natural/Analysis floor intersections, the CPU tracer, and the WebGPU tracer now all take the receiver height from OpticalScene instead of mixing a fixed visible floor with a shape-derived caustic floor; the previous 0.223 shape-unit plane mismatch displaced evening hits by about 0.61 unit. Unresolved outer-interface TIR no longer deposits receiver energy. The author-facing Natural composite temporarily gates focused light with the same finite-source transmission support as the visible transparent shadow. This is the first slice of the shared receiver-transport plan; peak-normalized 8-bit caustic fields still need replacement by fixed-domain HDR flux and an energy ledger. Production build and both WebGPU 65,536-ray and forced-safe CPU 88-ray Natural views passed.

Reorganized Cloud Sculpt and Hikari into a conventional application shell. Contextual Open, Save, and Export actions plus the workspace switch and fullscreen mode stay in a non-scrolling top bar. A Rhino-like right dock separates scene Layers from collapsible Properties, while fullscreen hides the chrome but retains an exit control. At 700px and below the dock moves under the viewport without introducing page scroll. Added an explicit same-resin inclusion action after the author observed that a low-IOR separate inclusion did not match the Ref Blender study; it aligns inner/outer IOR and leaves absorption contrast as the variable.

Added the first one-action Hikari-to-Blender handoff. The Hikari panel exports a watertight author-scaled OBJ, topology-check STL, shape recipe, Hikari case, and strict Blender study sidecar with SHA-256 hashes. Sidecar v2 explicitly maps Hikari right-handed Y-up coordinates to Blender right-handed Z-up as (x,y,z)→(x,-z,y), carries camera aspect/FOV, receiver, host/inclusion media, sun direction/angular diameter, and separates primary from check assets. Added a Blender bootstrap that reconstructs the scene without clearing existing work unless requested; the first analytic spherical inclusion may be generated when no mesh exists.

Connected reproducible Tokyo daylight to the Hikari runtime. A Tokyo civil date and time now resolve to a three-dimensional NOAA-style solar azimuth/altitude; the WebGL body/environment and CPU/WebGPU focused-light paths share that direction. Scrubbing time rebuilds the optical result, and direct sun/caustics stop below the horizon while sky light remains. Manual angle remains as an explicit fallback. Added renderer-independent room/multiple-window admission geometry and a strict Blender study sidecar contract as foundations; room apertures are not rendered yet.

Extended the WebGPU focused-light tracer through the first valid analytic spherical inclusion using the same OpticalScene adapter and containment gate as CPU. Completed rays refract host-to-inclusion-to-host, remarch the host exit, and apply approximate host/inclusion absorption plus interface losses; incomplete or TIR nested paths retain the established host-only result. Verified WGSL compilation and a 65,536-ray run on Apple metal-3. Added pure deterministic foundations for object-local pigment concentration variation and Tokyo solar position; neither is connected to the runtime controls yet.

Extended the CPU focused-light tracer through the first valid spherical inclusion. Completed paths refract host-to-inclusion-to-host, remarch the host exit, and deposit at the receiver from the final direction; incomplete or TIR paths preserve the established host-only result. CPU caustics are shown for inclusions, while WebGPU inclusion caustics remain suppressed until its path follows the same scene contract. Added a pure deterministic multi-inclusion generator contract for later runtime connection and documented object-local pigment concentration fields for intentional color variation.

Connected the first colored-host and clear-inclusion study to Hikari. Added reproducible host presets and inclusion controls, a runtime OpticalScene adapter, a pure straight-ray CPU reference with ordered medium events/RGB absorption/Fresnel throughput, and an analytic one-sphere inclusion in the WebGL body and transparent-shadow paths. Invalid containment falls back to the host with a visible warning. Existing CPU/WebGPU focused-light output is suppressed while the inclusion is active until it follows the same scene contract. The first runtime inclusion is deliberately one sphere; deterministic multiple random shapes and sizes are designed as the next generalization.

Added Phase 2 pure scene/geometry contracts for a single host and at most one inclusion. The contracts preserve medium identity independent of equal IOR, use quaternion-normalized uniform-scale poses, classify epsilon boundaries as air, and deterministically report containment witnesses. No renderer, shader, Hikari settings, CPU optics, or WebGPU optics behavior changed.

Added Phase 1 runtime-independent optical scene contracts: RGB Beer-Lambert material presets, explicit physical-scale provenance, legacy scalar-to-per-mm conversion, and pure optical-depth/transmission helpers. The assumed 1 mm/shape-unit reference is deliberately marked assumed, not a measured object size. Added four fixed Phase 0 baseline-case specifications. No Hikari runtime, renderer, shader, CPU optics, or WebGPU optics behavior changed.

Added versioned Hikari case capture. A case records the replayable shape recipe, full Hikari settings, orbit camera target/position, app version, compatibility/backend snapshot, and an optional observation note. Loading validates the schema before restoring the same view; this is a reproducible observation baseline, not a rendered-image export.

Separated the receiver's transparent shadow from its focused caustic after the author observed that the shadow disappeared and the light pool exposed a rectangular texture domain. The finite caustic field now has generous empty margins, CPU and shader edge feathering, a rounded outer support, and wider low-sample reconstruction for the Windows-safe 56-ray path. Natural-floor ambient light now retains a thickness-dependent translucent shadow under the caustic, while peak compression prevents the focused contribution from bleaching it away. Verified an irregular soft light pool inside a readable projected shadow in full WebGPU 16,384-ray and Windows-safe CPU 56-ray views with no rendering errors.

Added Both alongside Prism and Stress. Both evaluates the five-band prism refraction first, then applies stress-dependent wavelength phase and polarization on the same transmitted color; the receiver keeps the prism caustic while stress remains localized inside the form. Both exposes Prism Local/Global plus Cure Stress and Polarization together. Verified that Polarization 0 removes only the Stress contribution and leaves Local Prism visible, restoring polarization adds the junction/thickness interference bands, and the Windows-safe CPU 56-ray path renders the combined view without a black screen. Full WebGPU 16,384-ray and safe paths both passed visual checks.

Reworked prism color from three isolated RGB channels into a five-band red/amber/green/cyan/blue spectrum. Secondary wavelengths use lightweight environment samples, are normalized to remain neutral under uniform illumination, and amplify only inter-band environment differences; the floor field now deposits five overlapping spectral bands, producing a broader low-saturation gradient instead of thin digital red/blue fringes. Added an independent Stress rainbow model with Cure Stress and Polarization controls. Stress estimates shell competition at metaball junctions, internal path thickness, and material variation, then evaluates five wavelength-dependent phase delays to form localized photoelastic-like bands. Polarization 0 removes the stress color while preserving refraction. Prism-only and Stress-only controls now hide correctly. Verified Prism Global/Local, Stress at polarization 0 and 0.62, full WebGPU 16,384-ray, and Windows-safe CPU 56-ray paths with no black screen. This Stress mode is an exploratory proxy field, not a solved cure mechanics tensor.

Split resin rainbows into Local and Global modes after the author observed that real resin showed only occasional partial color. Global preserves the previous expressive whole-object visualizer. Local gates shape dispersion by outgoing bend, entry/exit normal change, and grazing incidence, and gates receiver RGB separation by refracted-ray deviation; most light therefore remains neutral while strongly redirected paths can form isolated fringes. The caustic rebuild signature now includes dispersion value and mode, fixing an earlier omission where slider changes updated the shader but did not rebuild RGB receiver positions. Verified Local/Global at Prism 1, Local mono, full WebGPU 16,384-ray, and Windows-safe CPU 56-ray paths with no rendering errors. Local is an optical-path approximation, not yet a cure-stress birefringence model.

Added the first wavelength-dispersion model for resin prism rainbows. A new Prism control offsets red and blue refractive indices around the central green path, so the infinite environment is sampled along three slightly different outgoing directions rather than receiving a screen-space color fringe. CPU/WebGPU receiver hits now become RGB-separated floor samples along each ray's bend direction, are accumulated into a shared-normalization RGB irradiance texture, and are sampled through the resin together with the floor. Low values stay subtle; the upper range deliberately exaggerates separation for observation. Color Prism 0/1, mono Prism 1, full WebGPU 16,384-ray, and Windows-safe CPU 56-ray paths were visually compared; the production build passed. This is a performant three-channel approximation with one shared exit point and central GPU trace, not a full spectral path tracer, thin-film interference, or stress birefringence.

Promoted caustics from a foreground point overlay into a 128x128 receiver irradiance field. CPU/WebGPU floor hits are bilinearly accumulated, lightly blurred, density-thresholded, and uploaded as a floor-space texture. Natural mode samples that field inside the same floor shader used by direct and refracted view rays, so a caustic seen through the resin is refracted again with the floor instead of being drawn on top; the old point layer remains Analysis-only. Added distance fog that converges the finite receiver toward the infinite sky, a 0-1 environment mist control that suppresses scenic detail near the horizon, and color/mono optical output. Verified full WebGPU 16,384-ray and Windows-safe 56-ray paths, mist 0.72/0.90, real mono click, and a lower camera view. Production build passed. Next optical phenomenon recorded from author observation: RGB wavelength dispersion for resin prism rainbows, kept distinct from thin-film interference and stress birefringence.

Restored receiver light in the full WebGPU path after the author observed that `?safe=0` no longer showed a caustic. The five oriented micro-deposits per refracted floor hit had been normalized by their expanded vertex count, making Natural exposure nearly vanish. Normalization now uses the number of rays that actually reach the receiver, and the Natural core/halo exposure was raised without changing the refraction positions. Verified in full-quality mode on M4: 16,384 rays with 4,107 shape hits again produce a concentrated, stretched, irregular light pool inside the transparent shadow. Production build passed.

Corrected the optical scene after the author annotated two artifacts: the finite nearby backdrop produced an impossible triangular boundary, and the Windows-safe 56-ray regular grid appeared as undistorted circular light dots. Removed the nearby plane/cylinder lookup and restored the backdrop as a strictly infinite directional environment; only the shape and receiver floor remain finite. Added broad non-grid floor illumination so refracted floor lookups are legible. CPU ray origins now use a low-discrepancy 2D sequence instead of rows, and each refracted floor hit becomes five oriented, stretched micro-deposits based on outgoing deviation. In forced safe mode, real UI comparison at IOR 1.10 and 1.65 changed both the environment bending and receiver light distribution. Production build passed.

Added an automatic Windows safe startup path after the author's entire page remained black, indicating a likely GPU-process stall rather than a local fragment-only error. Windows now uses pixel ratio 1, center-only rough reflection/refraction and transparent-shadow sampling, and temporarily keeps the raw WebGPU optical compute engine off in favor of the 56-ray CPU preview. The RTX path remains available for staged re-enablement. `?safe=1` forces the path on any OS and `?safe=0` explicitly bypasses it on Windows. Forced-safe rendering was visually verified on M4 with the full UI, transparent body, nearby-scene distortion, and central transmitted shadow visible; production build passed.

Compatibility patch after the author observed a black viewport on Windows. The v0.9 shader evaluated procedural material noise during every transparent-shadow march step and recomputed finite-source shadows for each rough environment offset. Material density is now evaluated at seven positions across the completed inside segment, while only the central reflection/refraction sample performs the expensive transparent-shadow query. Nearby-environment distortion, heterogeneous absorption, and the central soft transparent shadow remain. Reverified visible output on M4 and a successful production build; Windows hard-refresh confirmation is pending.

Made refraction spatially legible by replacing the direction-only distant backdrop with origin-aware nearby geometry: a z=-6 scenic plane and radius-8 cylindrical surroundings. Rays now leave the SDF exit point and intersect that environment, so its trunks and value boundaries visibly shift and bend through the shape; IOR 1.10 versus 1.65 and environment rotation 0 versus 70 degrees were compared through real UI input. Added GGX-like rough highlights, adaptive 3/5-sample rough reflection and transmission, procedural surface-normal variation, and a separated 3D material field that modulates both body absorption and transparent shadows. A rough heterogeneous resin setting ran around 19–21 fps on M4. Production build passed. Remaining limits are explicit: no HDRI/path tracing, multiple internal bounce, editable volume field, or progressive GPU accumulation; high roughness may reveal the small directional sample set.

Replaced Natural's binary single-direction ground shadow with finite-source transparent shadow sampling. Depending on source spread, 3/5/9 directions estimate partial visibility; each ray integrates approximate distance inside the shared SDF and applies Beer-Lambert spectral attenuation plus two-interface Fresnel transmission. Added an interactive 0.1–30 degree source-spread control with 0.53 degrees documented as clear-sun scale and larger values explicitly treated as a cloud/window/diffuser proxy rather than exact sky lighting. Verified by real UI input: 0.5 degrees retained a tighter shadow, 30 degrees produced a broad penumbra, and absorption 0.55→2.5 deepened thickness-dependent gradients. M4 measured about 23–26 fps for the 3-sample clear-sun case and about 13 fps for the 9-sample widest source; no shader errors.

Added the first WebGPU compute path for Hikari Optics while preserving the WebGL renderer and CPU fallback. SDF entry/exit intersection and refraction now process 4,096–131,072 optical samples on a high-performance adapter; computed samples are independent from the 8–120 visible diagnostic rays. The UI reports the actual backend, browser-exposed adapter identity, sample/hit counts, readback-complete time, and throughput. On M4/metal-3, 16,384 samples produced 1,841 shape hits in about 2.0 ms; 65,536 produced 7,554 hits in about 118–170 ms after warm-up. Density and caustic alpha are normalized by visualized sample count to avoid sample-count-driven whiteout. Verified Analysis/Natural and ray OFF with real UI interactions.

Added Natural / Analysis optics views. Natural combines hemispherical sky light, directional sun, a matte receiver with nonzero ambient fill, approximate SDF sun occlusion, ground reflectance, exposure, and reduced caustic overlay so shadow and concentration read as deviations inside an already lit environment. Analysis preserves the dark optical-density view. Verified real-coordinate switching, ray overlay OFF, and interactive sky/sun values with no shader errors.

Changed optical ray visualization from the mutually exclusive Rays/Density/Both selector to an independent ray overlay toggle. Density and caustic computation now remain visible while the sampled ray lines turn OFF/ON. Legacy 'rays' and 'both' values migrate to ON; 'density' and old 'surface' migrate to OFF. Verified both toggle states with real-coordinate clicks.

Author feedback rejected the Sun wavefront planes and studio grid as visually attached explanatory scaffolding. Replaced Surface with a Flow-Density-like additive optical deposition: soft particles accumulate along incident, internal, and outgoing paths, while the matte environment no longer draws a grid. The old saved 'surface' value migrates to 'density'. Rays/Density/Both and the denser overlapping result were visually verified.

Hikari Optics v0.3 makes the directional Sun source visible as moving wavefront surfaces instead of only sampled rays. Added Rays/Surface/Both display modes and interactive light-field width; the same finite source plane still seeds the refraction and receiver-plane accumulation. Verified all display modes and width 1.00→1.55 in the browser with no rendering errors.

Added Hikari Optics v0.2 beside Flow. The same Cloud Sculpt SDF now drives a realtime water/glass view shader plus CPU-traced parallel rays through entry and exit refraction, with additive deposits on a receiver plane. Water/glass, IOR, light angle, ray count, absorption, and caustic strength are interactive and browser-persisted. Visually verified that rerolling Katachi immediately rebuilds the optical paths and light deposits without file transfer.

Added the first Hikari observation view directly inside Cloud Sculpt. KATACHI and HIKARI read the same in-memory ball field and camera without export/import. Hikari provides deterministic surface/inside particle sampling, Points/Trails/Density views, and interactive controls persisted by the browser. Build passed and all three views plus both spawn modes were visually verified in the local browser.
